Cc: infra-team@acme-corp.com
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC TLS resilience + internal DNS primer

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. We’re mapping out our private deployment checklist for the Acme VPC (on-prem edge + cloud peering) and want to lock down DNS and TLS responsibilities before the pilot. A few asks where we need Redwood’s input: 

1) Certificate sourcing: we’d prefer a customer-managed cert for the tenant-facing private FQDNs (internal.acme), but we need guidance on CSR format and recommended SANs for service discovery and telemetry.
2) TLS termination boundary: proposal is to terminate TLS at our ingress LB and use mTLS between the LB and Redwood private runtime. Curious if Redwood supports short-lived certs / ACME integration for the runtime side.
3) DNS resilience: we plan a split-horizon setup, and want patterns for resolver failover across peered VPCs.

Attaching a rough diagram of our current DNS/peering topology (acme-internal-dns-diagram.png). Can we run a short call early next week to align on the minimal artifacts you’ll need (CSRs, proof-of-control, OCSP expectations)?

Thanks,
Tim
Infrastructure Eng, Acme Corp

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Timothy Harris <timothy.harris@acme-corp.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, infra-team@acme-corp.com
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC TLS resilience + internal DNS primer

Tim —

Appreciate the diagram, that helps. Quick responses inline and an ask for a short checklist we can provide as artifacts: 

1) Certificate sourcing:
- We can support either customer-managed certs (you upload PEM + chain) or a joint model where Acme manages external-facing certs and Redwood mints runtime certs from a designated intermediate.
- For customer-managed certs, CSR template attached (redwood-csr-sample.txt). Recommended SANs: primary FQDN, *.internal.acme for wildcard where needed, and a URI SAN for service identity if you use SPIFFE.

2) TLS termination boundary:
- Terminating at your ingress LB is fine. Our recommended pattern is: customer LB terminates external client TLS -> TLS re-encrypt to an internal service FQDN -> Redwood runtime accepts mTLS (client auth) using a cert issued by your PKI or a mutually-trusted CA.
- If you want runtime-side short-lived certs, we offer an ACME-like provisioning integration for private roots (requires a trust anchor exchange and proof-of-possession). Details below.

3) DNS resilience / split-horizon:
- Typical pattern: internal resolvers in each VPC -> conditional forwarders to the authoritative internal zone -> fallback to peer resolver IPs with low TTLs.
- We recommend health-checked SRV records for runtime endpoints so your LB can prefer healthy runtime replicas across AZs/peers.

Checklist we need from Acme before pilot:
- Primary tenant FQDNs + desired SAN list
- CSR or public certs (PEM) for customer-managed mode OR CA trust anchor for Redwood-issued certs
- A short contact list for OCSP/CRL callback and a maintenance window for test rotation

I’ll put together a tightened one-page primer and a sample proof-of-possession flow for your security team. Looping in Kim (certs/ops) to clarify the ACME/private-root path.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700

Rishi / Tim —

Solid starting point. A few clarifying notes from cert ops that will affect automation and our ask list: 

- If Acme chooses customer-managed certs: we will only accept PEM bundles (private key never transmitted). Redwood will validate chain and perform OCSP stapling checks at startup; we will need the issuer CN and the OCSP responder URL at onboarding.

- If Acme prefers Redwood-issued runtime certs (recommended for short-lived certs/rotation): we need a trust anchor exchange (PEM of your root/intermediate) and a per-tenant CSR-signing policy. We can expose a non-public ACME endpoint that validates either DNS TXT proof (for split-horizon we support an out-of-band HTTP token proof) or an API-based proof-of-possession through a signed JWT from your PKI.

- DNS: make sure the internal authoritative name servers have a second internal IP in each AZ for quick failover. For SRV/health: our runtime health endpoints will return an instance-level boolean; we recommend your LB use that for active/passive decisions (TTL 5-15s for SRV).

- Audit / SOC2 evidence: please provide the signed CSR transaction logs (or ACME audit entries) for the pilot window so our compliance team can tie issuance events to your control plane.

Attached: brief ops checklist for both modes (I’ll send as PDF to the shared drive).

Kim
Certs & Ops, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the draft alignment. This looks good for the pilot track; two operational asks before we sign off: 

1) Produce the one-page primer Rishi mentioned and include the exact CSR fields we will accept plus a minimal test matrix (rotate cert, failover resolver, verify OCSP stapling). I want that in the shared drive by EOD Monday so Security can include it in the onboarding package.

2) Kim: can you produce a small template for the ACME audit entries we’ll provide to customers (one example for DNS TXT proof + one for API-signed JWT)? Security needs examples for SOC2 intake.

Tim, once we have the primer + audit templates we’ll schedule a 30-min runbook walkthrough and a short maintenance window for handshake testing.

Thanks,
